https://www.dw.com/en/pakistan-suicide-b.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Mqgi Attackers stormed the Old Police Lines complex at Kohat, a town of around 220,000 people in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province Image: REUTERS Advertisement The death toll from a suicide bombing in Kohat, Pakistan , near the Afghan border, has risen to at least 31 people, police said on Saturday, as fighting continued to rage. Militants stormed the district police headquarters complex at Kohat in Pakistan's northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province on Friday. An explosives-laden car caused a large explosion and severely damaged a mosque on a police compound. "At least 31 people, including 16 police personnel, have been killed and more than 100 injured so far in the militant attack and suicide bombing," a police official told AFP on Saturday. "Several militants are still holed up in the Special Branch section of the Kohat Police Complex. An exchange of fire with them has been ongoing since late last night. Their exact number remains unclear." Pakistan has blamed the surge in attacks on militancy emanating from Afghanistan Image: Hussain Ali/ZUMA/picture alliance What do we know about the attack in Kohat? Police said in a statement that the suicide attack occurred near a mosque as officers, their relatives and other civilians were worshipping inside. The statement added that security forces engaged other militants in a subsequent gun battle after at least two other attackers tried to to enter the facility. Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, a local militant group linked to the Pakistani Taliban, Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) , has claimed responsibility for the attack. Kohat, a city of around 220,000 people south of Peshawar, is fairly close to the Afghan border Image: B.S. Gillani/AP Photo/picture alliance Government blames TTP amid attack in Afghan border area Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack and expressed sorrow over the casualties. He directed authorities to accelerate rescue operations. Pakistan's Interior Ministry said that the "cowardly actions" of the attackers would not weaken "the nation's resolve." President Asif Ali Zardari appeared to blame the Pakistani Taliban, or TTP (Tehreek-e-Taliban). "The complete elimination of Fitna-al-Khawarij and terrorists operating with foreign backing is essential for national security," Zardari said, using another term for the TTP. Pakistan blames Afghanistan for surge in violence The attack comes at a time when relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan's Taliban rulers are already fraught. Islamabad accuses the TTP uses safe havens across the Afghan border to plot and train for attacks in Pakistan. Pakistan blames the increase of attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the border province of Balochistan further south in large part on the Taliban administration in neighboring Afghanistan. How 5 years of Taliban rule have changed Afghanistan To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The Taliban rejects these allegations. The accusations have sparked a bitter rift and even incidents of armed conflict between the neighboring countries . Pakistan has carried out airstrikes it says targets militants taking refuge on Afghan soil, including this June . Authorities in Kabul have in turn decried these attacks and reported civilian casualties. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/20/fran.text: Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani welcomed French President Emmanuel Macron with full state honours, including cannon salvos and a cavalry procession, as he began his two-day state visit to the Gulf nation on Tuesday.After the official welcome ceremony, the two leaders met at Lusail Palace to discuss strengthening strategic ties between France and Qatar, including energy security, defence and regional stability, as well as investments and cooperation in multiple fields.Macron was received at Hamad International Airport by Qatar’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of State for Defence Affairs, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman bin Hassan Al Thani, after fighter jets escorted his plane on arrival as part of the state visit honours, followed by a state motorcade procession through Doha towards Lusail.Macron's state visit to Qatar concludes his regional Gulf tour to develop strategic partnerships also with the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait and Bahrain, where the French leader secured pledges of additional energy supplies from Gulf partners.The tour has already produced commitments for additional diesel. The French presidency said France had secured pledges for an extra 200,000 tonnes a month from the UAE and Bahrain, around 100,000 tonnes from each.Including supplies from Saudi Arabia, the commitments totalled 295,000 tonnes a month, equivalent to just over 10% of French consumption, the Élysée said.In a speech to the French nation on Sunday after a weekend of violent protests that engulfed France, Macron said he would travel to the Gulf countries to secure France’s energy supplies and to address the grievances over fuel prices and the cost of living, while his government worked with fuel distributors to ensure those efforts translated into lower prices for consumers.Energy security and regional tiesMacron is accompanied by French business leaders including the chief executives of France's largest energy companies, TotalEnergies and Engie. TotalEnergies already has substantial interests in Qatar, including a partnership with QatarEnergy in the North Field East LNG expansion project, one of the world's largest.Qatar’s foreign ministry said Tuesday’s talks would be followed by a strategic dialogue on Wednesday to discuss "many regional matters of mutual concern,” covering energy, the economy, investment and defence.Speaking at a briefing in Doha, the ministry’s director of media and communication, Ibrahim bin Sultan Al Hashmi, described France as a friend and ally and underlined its position during the ongoing regional crisis.France was among Qatar's main defenders during the Iran war, securing the Gulf country's air defence with fighter jets and other capabilities and is now seeking to develop additional defence ties.The visit also builds on wider investment ties. During the Emir’s 2024 state visit to France, Qatar pledged €10 billion in investment across sectors including energy transition, artificial intelligence, aerospace, and healthcare.
